title: Private deploy networking incident notes - VPC peering / DNS / TLS / egress
content:
Summary:
- Short incident notes while debugging customer private deploy (staging) where model-serving instances could not reach Redwood control-plane endpoints and customers reported TLS failures to our provisioner. Intermittent; started ~2026-03-02 09:10 UTC, ongoing.
notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-02 09:10 UTC: automated alerts - failed healthchecks from customer nodes to control-plane (connectivity errors).
- 2026-03-02 09:25 UTC: first on-call triage - symptoms show DNS failures + TLS handshake errors on some AZs.
- 2026-03-02 10:00 UTC: opened JIRA-PRIVNET-783, looped in Maya, Noah.
- 2026-03-03: additional incidents in other staging clusters, similar symptoms.
- 2026-03-04 07:30 UTC: found inconsistent route propagation on peering connection and stale DNS resolver config on some instances.
observed_symptoms:
- curl to control-plane: 'curl: (7) Failed to connect to <control-plane-host> port 443: Connection timed out' on some nodes but success on others.
- openssl s_client returned certificate verify failed on certain nodes: '140A90B1:SSL routines:ssl3_get_server_certificate:certificate verify failed'.
- dig returns NXDOMAIN intermittently for internal hostnames in customer VPC from affected nodes.
- Traceroute shows packets black-holing at peering target in specific AZ subnets.
- No obvious CPU/memory issues on the instances themselves.
what_i_tried_commands_and_outputs:
Commands run (copied snippets):
1) ip route and route table checks on affected instance:
$ ip route show
default via 10.0.0.1 dev eth0 proto dhcp metric 100
10.0.0.0/16 dev eth0 proto kernel scope link src 10.0.1.45

2) traceroute to control-plane:
$ traceroute -n 34.123.56.78
 1 10.0.1.1 0.3 ms 0.2 ms 0.3 ms
 2 172.31.255.254 * * *
 3 * * *

(note: hop 2 is the peering/gateway IP that drops)

3) dig for internal service: 
$ dig +short service.internal.redwood
; on affected node => (empty)
; on unaffected node => 10.240.3.12

4) curl verbose TLS failure:
$ curl -v https://control-plane.internal/health
* Connected to control-plane.internal (34.123.56.78) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* error:140A90B1:SSL routines:ssl3_get_server_certificate:certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: certificate verify failed

5) openssl s_client debug against IP and hostname:
$ openssl s_client -connect 34.123.56.78:443 -servername control-plane.internal -showcerts
...
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate

6) tcpdump on peering interface (brief):
14:12:35.123456 IP 10.0.1.45.52344 > 34.123.56.78.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 12345 ecr 0], length 0
14:12:35.223456 IP 10.0.1.45.52344 > 34.123.56.78.443: Flags [S], seq 0, ack 1, length 0
(no SYN-ACK from intermediate gateway in some captures)

7) Check VPC peering and route tables in console:
- peering connection status: Active
- route table of customer VPC: missing route for control-plane prefix in one of the AZ subnets (stale automation didn't push update)
- peering route propagation: sometimes not present if route table was modified outside IaC

8) Security group checks:
- SG on instances allow outbound 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 443 (ok)
- SG on control-plane side allow inbound from peer CIDR (ok)

9) NAT / egress checks:
- instances in private subnets use NAT gateway in same AZ; NAT gateway healthy. However, nodes that failed were in a subnet that routes to a transit gateway that had missing propagation to peering target.

10) DNS resolver config:
- /etc/resolv.conf on affected nodes pointed at custom resolver 10.0.2.2 (legacy) which returned NXDOMAIN for internal names in some AZs.
- Switching to VPC provided resolver (169.254.169.253 or 10.0.0.2 depending on cloud) immediately resolved names on test node.
hypotheses:
1) Primary hypothesis: stale/misconfigured route in a subset of route tables for certain AZ subnets causing packets to be routed to a gateway that drops/black-holes traffic to control-plane. Route automation failed during a recent subnet change.
2) Secondary: mixed DNS resolver config across instances - some still using customer-provided resolver that doesn't forward internal zones; combined with route issues this looks intermittent.
3) TLS errors are largely downstream effects of connecting to wrong IP (internal middlebox) or failing SNI / certificate mismatch when traffic is routed to a proxy.
4) Less likely: security group or NACL change, but checks so far show rules are permissive for outbound.
root_cause_findings:
- Missing route for control-plane prefix in route table for az-a-subnet-3. IaC drift caused route not to be added.
- Some instances were using legacy DNS resolver (10.0.2.2) because of an older bootstrap script; that resolver returned NXDOMAIN for .internal names.
- As a result some nodes tried to talk to fallback IPs (or timed out) and raised TLS verify errors because they hit our egress proxy with a different cert chain.
mitigation_and_fixes_done:
- Manually added missing route to the problematic route table (temporary fix) using console and confirmed traceroute now reaches control-plane from previously affected nodes.
- Updated /etc/resolv.conf on one test node to use the VPC resolver and verified dig returns internal host IPs.
- Rolled a quick automation patch to IaC to re-apply missing route to all affected subnets (PR created: https://github.com/redwood/ops/pull/456).
- Notified customer and scheduled controlled rollout of permanent fix.
next_steps_and_follow_up:
- Audit all route tables across customer private deployment for IaC drift and add guardrails (enforce via terraform plan check in pipeline).
- Patch bootstrap scripts to ensure resolver config uses VPC resolver by default; add a healthcheck that queries an internal name at boot.
- Add automated synthetic check from each AZ that performs: dig service.internal, curl https://control-plane/health, traceroute to control-plane; alert if mismatch between AZs.
- Postmortem: prepare timeline + RCA and share with customer and internal SRE. Owner: Arjun Singh. Target publish date: 2026-03-06.
- Follow-up ticket: JIRA-PRIVNET-790 for resolver bootstrap fix, JIRA-PRIVNET-791 for route table guardrails.
notes_to_self:
- When reproducing, capture tcpdump from both sides of peering connection (customer side and our peering gateway).
- Consider adding an agent on provisioning that asserts /etc/resolv.conf contains vpc resolver or fails provisioning.
- Investigate whether transit gateway route propagation settings can be locked or alerted for changes.
- Double-check certificate chains presented by our egress proxies to ensure we can distinguish proxy vs control-plane failures in logs.
- Save relevant captures to S3: s3://redwood-incident-capture/privnet-2026-03
